target_customer: Travel agencies, travel startups, fintechs and spend management apps that want to sell flights, and later hotels, through one API
problem: Airline booking systems are accessed through legacy intermediaries such as Sabre and Amadeus, which are complex and expensive. Duffel offers a modern API to search, book and manage flights directly with airlines.
business_model: Usage-based API: fees per booking plus ancillary and commission revenue

founders.name: Steve Domin
founders.background_notes: Sole founder on the YC page, called co-founder and CEO by TechCrunch (October 2019). No co-founder named in opened sources. Background not found.

technical_complexity.rationale: Integrating many airline systems, handling fares, ticketing, payments and order changes through one reliable API is hard integration work.

defensibility.rationale: Direct airline connections, certifications and developer integrations take years to build, but airlines and legacy distributors can offer APIs.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: TechCrunch in October 2019 contrasts Duffel with Sabre and Amadeus. No source found of them copying or buying it. Duffel cut about a fifth of staff in September 2022 and remains independent.

market_need_then: Airlines were shifting to direct distribution standards such as NDC, and new digital travel agencies needed easier access than GDS contracts. No 2018 dated spend figures were found.

identity.voice_and_tone: Plain pitch: Sell travel, without the complexity

branding.brand_signature: The best API to sell travel tagline
branding.community_and_virality: No evidence of community or merch found. Active on Product Hunt per search results.

brand_strength.rationale: Memorable travel word that fits the bag metaphor, developer friendly voice, customers named on site. Duffel bag is also a common word, with spelling variance (duffle).

outcome_analysis: Duffel raised $21.5M in June 2019 and a $30M Series B led by Index Ventures in October 2019, with airline partners including American, British Airways and Lufthansa. It cut about a fifth of staff in September 2022 during the downturn but stayed independent. It now serves customers like Rippling and TravelBank with about 55 staff.
notes: The June 2019 round comes from a PhocusWire snippet (Series B coverage stated a 21.5M raise in June and total 56M), the article itself returned 403. Investors of that round not stated, one aggregator names Benchmark as lead, unverified. Index backed Duffel since seed per TechCrunch, but the seed amount is not found, CB Insights dates first funding 2018-08, unverified. Total raised about 56M per PhocusWire and CB Insights. Competitors: TechCrunch names Sabre and Amadeus in 2019 (over a year after the batch), so not listed per the as_of rule, and guides found are current year. Layoff figure of about 18 people comes from a Daily Telegraph piece via PressReader.
